title: Act 0 — Get in from Cloud Terminal
explain: You are on the RHDP bastion through the Cloud Terminal browser terminal. This is the starting point for the whole workshop. We check the assigned AWS account, the existing ROSA cluster, administrator access, and CPU worker capacity before the GPU and platform labs. This deployed lab already has its model; do not provision a second cluster or change billing.
question: What should you use as the starting environment?

choices.B: Use the existing assigned RHDP cluster and bastion
choices.C: Switch to a personal Red Hat organization

hint: The facilitator has already assigned the environment and its billing setup.

title: Lab 1.1 — GPU machine pool
explain: This existing ROSA cluster has CPU workers for platform services and a GPU worker for Qwen3.8 inference. The NoSchedule GPU taint reserves scarce GPU capacity for pods with the matching toleration. We inspect it; there is no need to create another pool.
question: Which workload needs the NVIDIA GPU in this workshop?

choices.A: Serving the Fortune Cookie HTML page

hint: Think about the workload that performs matrix computations when OpenCode answers.

title: Lab 1.2 — Install platform operators
explain: Operators manage the serving platform and developer tools. The DataScienceCluster declares the desired OpenShift AI components. A Ready condition tells us that a controller reconciled them; it does not yet prove that a developer can call the model.
question: Why use an operator instead of installing a controller once by hand?

choices.A: It removes all need for CPU workers
choices.B: It replaces Git with the cluster database
choices.C: It continuously reconciles the declared configuration

hint: Consider what should happen after a controller pod is restarted.

title: Lab 1.3 — Publish Qwen3.8 as a service
source: Lab 1.3 and Lab 2.1 — Publish and call Qwen3.8
explain: OpenCode sends OpenAI-compatible requests to Qwen3.8 on this cluster. MaaS authenticates its injected API key and applies the subscription's token quota. We test both model discovery and an actual completion, without displaying the key.
question: What does MaaS add in front of the inference service?

choices.A: Authenticated model access and token quotas

hint: The same model is shared by developers; consider who may call it and how much they may consume.

title: Lab 1.4 — Hand the keys
explain: The platform engineer hands the developer a Dev Spaces launch URL and the Go template. AGENTS.md contains the generation and delivery rules; opencode.json selects the in-cluster model. The workshop companion stays here in Cloud Terminal while the participant later opens the coding workspace.
question: What guides the coding agent when generating and shipping the application?

choices.B: The project AGENTS.md and prepared template

hint: Look at the runbook shipped with the Go app template.

title: Lab 2.1 — Launch the developer workspace
source: Lab 1.4 and Lab 2.1 — Launch Dev Spaces
explain: Now switch to the developer persona. Open the Dev Spaces launch URL, trust the template and workspace, then use its terminal for the coding exercise. The companion continues in the Cloud Terminal bastion and checks the workspace from there. Dev Spaces is one lab within this global workshop, not the companion host.
question: Where does this workshop's developer environment run?

choices.B: In a Dev Spaces workspace pod on the cluster
choices.C: On a required local Docker installation

hint: Your browser displays the editor, but the terminal commands execute somewhere else.
try_command: Open the Dev Spaces factory URL printed by the companion

title: Lab 2.2 — Prompt to production
source: Lab 2.2 — Plan, build, deploy, then ship a change
explain: In the developer workspace, follow the guide: plan the Fortune Cookie Go app, implement it in the same session, then ship a change. OpenCode follows AGENTS.md, Tekton builds an image and Argo CD deploys it. Return to this Cloud Terminal companion for explanations, questions and verification. In this existing lab the app is already deployed, so inspect its delivery evidence instead of rebuilding it automatically.
question: Which pairing describes the delivery workflow?

choices.A: Argo CD compiles Go; Tekton serves HTTP
choices.B: MaaS builds the image; Dev Spaces reconciles production
choices.C: Tekton builds the image; Argo CD reconciles the deployment

hint: Separate making an image from keeping the running application aligned with Git.

title: Lab 2.3 — Audit the application
explain: Ask the coding agent to check resource requests and limits, health probes, pod security and Route TLS. The global companion reads the resulting Deployment and Route to verify the workshop rules. Requests guide scheduling, limits cap consumption, and probes control health handling.
question: What should you verify before calling the deployed app ready?

choices.A: Resources, health probes, pod security and HTTPS
choices.B: Only that a Git repository exists
choices.C: Only that the GPU is busy

hint: A running pod alone does not prove that the workload follows the platform rules.

title: Lab 3.1 — GPU and token metrics
explain: DCGM measures GPU utilization and memory. vLLM exports prompt and generated token counters. GPU usage falls when no prompt is running; a zero reading does not imply a broken model. The MaaS subscription limits consumption, while metrics show observed usage.
question: Which measurements show this workshop's AI workload?

choices.A: DCGM GPU metrics and vLLM token counters
choices.B: Only requests to the Fortune Cookie route
choices.C: Only the number of Git commits

hint: The Go app serves fixed messages; the model does work when OpenCode generates a response.

title: Wrap-up — Explain the complete platform
explain: Connect the whole workshop: RHDP provides the base cluster and bastion; the GPU serves Qwen, MaaS governs access, Dev Spaces hosts the developer, Tekton builds, Argo CD reconciles, and DCGM/vLLM show consumption. Summarize what you would change for a team and which lab you would like to revisit.
question: Which sequence connects developer intent to a running app?

choices.A: MaaS builds images and DCGM deploys them
choices.B: OpenCode generates, Tekton builds, Argo CD reconciles
choices.C: The static Cloud Terminal page provisions the cluster

hint: Keep code generation, image construction and GitOps reconciliation distinct.
